title: Fix FP8 prefill alignment handling for long-context prompts + regression test
author: Grace Kim
description: Context: We saw intermittent correctness issues and occasional CUDA misaligned access faults in the FP8 prefill path when running long-context prompts (>=16k, most frequently 32k) on H100/H200 in perf-lab and in one customer reproduction (SUP-6194). Root cause: our FP8 prefill attention/GEMM launch config was computing K/V and Q tile alignment using a padded sequence length, but the pointer arithmetic for the packed FP8 layout still used the unpadded stride in one codepath. For certain (seq_len % alignment != 0) shapes, this could cause the kernel to read past the end of the logical prefill buffer (or into the next contiguous allocation) depending on allocator packing, which manifested as numerical drift for some prompts and rare hard faults. Fix: unify alignment and stride computation for FP8 prefill so that (1) the packed-layout stride uses the same padded length that the kernel expects, (2) we clamp loads for the tail block for safety, and (3) we add an explicit guard in the kernel selector to avoid choosing the FP8 prefill kernel variant when head_dim/seq_len fall into the unsupported tail pattern (falls back to FP16 prefill only for that phase, decode remains FP8). Added a targeted regression test covering long-context (32k) with an intentionally misaligned prompt length to exercise the tail block; the test compares FP8-vs-FP16 outputs on a small prompt set with a tight drift threshold and asserts no illegal memory access via compute-sanitizer in CI nightly. Perf: no measurable regression in prefill tokens/sec on the benchmark matrix; a small improvement (~0.3-0.6%) in p95 prefill latency for the long-context case due to removing an extra re-pack step that was happening on fallback. Rollout: gated behind existing quant mode flags; safe to ship in the next runtime train. Notes: This does not change FP8 format policy (see ADR), only fixes address calculation and adds a conservative selector guard.
commits: kernels/fp8: compute padded stride once and thread through prefill launch params
kernels/fp8: clamp tail loads for packed layout (prefill only)
runtime: selector guard for unsupported tail pattern (fallback to fp16 prefill)
tests: add long-context prefill alignment regression (32k, misaligned length)
docs: add troubleshooting note + repro command snippet for ENG-24815
release_notes: Bugfix: Fixed FP8 prefill alignment handling for long-context prompts to prevent rare numerical drift and misaligned access faults.
Added a targeted regression test for long-context FP8 prefill with misaligned sequence lengths.
conversation: Hiro Tanaka: Can you summarize why this only shows up on long-context and not the usual 2-4k prompt set? Grace Kim: The issue is in the tail block handling; for seq_len that crosses multiple tiles, the last tile is partial and we were mixing padded vs unpadded stride only for the prefill packed layout. Short prompts often end up fully aligned due to our common prompt templates and the selector choosing a different kernel variant. Noah Patel: The selector fallback seems conservative; are we risking perf cliffs for some customers? Grace Kim: The guard only triggers on the specific tail pattern we can’t safely clamp without changing the kernel ABI; in practice it’s a small subset (misaligned long prompts). Decode stays FP8. Isabella Rossi: Can we make the regression test deterministic and cheap? Also, can we add a reproducer to the benchmark harness? Grace Kim: Test uses a fixed seed prompt set and checks drift thresholds only on the affected shapes; it runs in GPU unit tests. I added a doc snippet with the repro command; harness integration is tracked in ENG-24811/ENG-24818. Jonas Weber: Drift threshold choice? Grace Kim: Using the same tolerance as the quant sanity suite for prefill logits; this change should reduce drift, not increase it. CI note: First run failed in compute-sanitizer due to an unrelated timeout; reran after raising the sanitizer step timeout for this job only. Final approvals: Hiro approved after requesting one comment explaining padded stride derivation; Noah approved after seeing selector stats from perf-lab run; Isabella approved after test runtime stayed <2 minutes on H100.
